{{recipe}}

'''Potstickers''' (锅贴 鍋貼 guōtiē; literally "pot stick") are a Northern Chinese-style [[Cookbook:Dumpling|dumpling]] popular as a street food, appetizer, or side order in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Japan|Japanese]] and [[Cookbook:Cuisine of China|Chinese cuisine]]. This dish is often served on a [[Cookbook:Dim sum|dim sum]] menu, but may be offered independently. The filling for this dish usually contains [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] (or [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]]), [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]], [[Cookbook:Scallion|scallion]]s, [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], and [[Cookbook:Sesame Oil|sesame seed]] oil. The mixed filling is sealed into a dumpling wrapper, steamed in a [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]], and then fried to crispness on one side in a shallow frying pan. The effect of the one crisp side of the dumpling is where it gets its English name of potsticker as it appears to have been stuck to the pot in which it was cooked. The potsticker is similar to the Japanese [[Cookbook:Gyoza|gyoza]] dumpling.

Also see recipes for [[Cookbook:Gyoza]] and [[Cookbook:Pot Stickers]] (which has a nice pictorial).

== Ingredients ==
=== Filling ===
* ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] (about 250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) ground [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] or [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]
* ½ pound ground raw [[Cookbook:Shrimp|prawn or shrimp]]
* 12 raw prawns/shrimp, [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Water Chestnut|water chestnuts]] (fresh if possible) peeled and [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] light [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]]
* 1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Sesame Oil|sesame oil]]
* 1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Pepper|white pepper]] (optional)
* 3 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Green Onion|green/spring onion]], minced
* 3 tablespoons fresh [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], minced
* 3 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]], chopped

=== Assembly ===

* 1 package store-bought gyoza/wonton wrappers
* [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|Cornstarch]]
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]

== Procedure ==
# Mix together the filling ingredients.
# Place a small bowl of water on the work area. If desired, mix in a little cornstarch to make a glue.
# Lay out one of the gyoza wrappers in front of you.
# Dip your finger in the water and moisten the edges of the wrapper.
# Place a heaped [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] of filling in the middle of the wrapper.
# Fold the gyoza wrapper over the filling and pinch the edges to seal it shut.
# Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] or [[Cookbook:Wok|wok]].  
# When oil is ready, carefully add the dumplings and cook on high heat until golden brown (about 1 minute).
# Without turning the dumplings over, add 1 cup of water and cover.  
# [[Cookbook:Steaming|Steam]] for about 1 minute to cook the raw filling and then turn off the heat (this is to keep the bottom from burning).  
# Let the dumplings cook for a few more minutes with the heat turned off.  
# Serve the potstickers with dipping sauce or soy sauce.
